Recharge of the overburden unit in Tract III is from precipitation on the tract and from lateral flow from the southeast. Hydrographs of wells 4A and 5A indicate a seasonal response to precipitation. Discharge from the overburden unit is to springs and downward as recharge to deeper aquifers.
Rosebud-McKay Coal - The Rosebud-McKay coal is present over most of Tract III and in a small part of the central-western part of Tract II. It consists of 25 to 35 feet of cleated coal and includes a shale bed which is up to 36 inches thick on the eastern part of Tract III. The coal has burned over most of Tract II and the western and northern part of Tract III, leaving clinker areas.
The coal is saturated with ground water in the south and central parts of Tract III. In Tract II the coal (where present) is either unsaturated or only partially saturated. Hydrographs made from water level measurements in observation wells (Dames and Moore, 1975) indicate a seasonal response of potentiometric surfaces in the northern and central parts of Tract III and a subdued response in the southern part of the Tract. There, much of the recharge to the coal may be from lateral flow from the southeast.
Ground water occurs in fractures in the coal. Pumping tests on six wells in Tract III and one well in Tract II indicate a range of transmissivity of from 1 to 45 gpd/ft and a range in permeability of from 1 x 
10^{-6}

10^{-5}
